value.name: corrects letter formation
value.description: A speaker points out that the mother's handwritten D uses a loop while the current D does not.
evidence: My mother made a *D* with a loop. That *D* doesn't have a loop.

value.name: Lucia retrieves birthday cards
value.description: Lucia silently gets up, opens the sideboard drawer, and brings back a stack of birthday cards tied with a rubber band.
evidence: she got up from the table and went to the sideboard and opened the top drawer and took out a stack of birthday cards held together with a rubber band, and she came back and she sat down

value.name: Lucia reads birthday cards aloud
value.description: Lucia lays out four cards and reads the birthday messages aloud to Daniel, drawing attention to the handwritten Ds.
evidence: she undid the rubber band and she laid out four cards in front of him.
"*To my Daniel,*" she read aloud, from the first. "*To Daniel.* *Para Daniel.* *Daniel — happy birthday from your mother who loves you.* Look at the *D*s, Daniel. Look at them."

value.name: Daniel refuses to look
value.description: Daniel initially refuses to look at the cards when Lucia tells him to.

value.name: Daniel examines the cards
value.description: After Lucia repeats the command, Daniel looks and recognizes that the Ds match the letter in the cards.
evidence: The *D*s were the *D*s in the letter.

value.name: Daniel breaks down quietly
value.description: Daniel lowers his head to the table and releases a breath-like sound that suggests a private emotional collapse rather than crying.
evidence: He put his head down on the table.
he kept it there, and his shoulders did not shake, and after a moment Asha realized that what he was doing was something more private than crying.
He was making the sound a person makes when they have been holding their breath without knowing it and have suddenly remembered how to exhale.

value.name: Rosa comforts Daniel
value.description: Rosa reaches across the table and rests her hand on the back of Daniel's head in a silent gesture of comfort.
evidence: Rosa reached across the table and put her hand on the back of his head.
She did not say anything. She just put her hand there,

value.name: Rosa recalls past comfort
value.description: The narration links Rosa's touch to earlier moments when she likely comforted Daniel as a child and teenager after injuries and failure.
evidence: the way she had probably put her hand there when he had been six years old and had skinned his knee on the brick steps out front, the way she had probably put her hand there when he had been fourteen and had failed an algebra test
